title: Special Executive Programme In Supply Chain Management
description: This programme equips professionals with essential knowledge in planning, managing, and optimizing supply chain operations for organizational success.
longDescription: The Special Executive Programme in Supply Chain Management offers a comprehensive study of planning models, inventory control, risk management, and quality improvement tools. Participants will gain expertise in the principles, tools, and technologies necessary for efficient and resilient supply chains.
courseDetails: Understand Supply Chain Planning (SCP) and its pivotal role in organizational success. Explore the tangible benefits derived from effective Supply Chain Planning. Identify key planning areas crucial for streamlined operations in the supply chain. Comprehend the significance of forecasting demand within the supply chain. Examine the criteria utilized in forecasting processes for enhanced accuracy. Acquire knowledge of a systematic approach to forecasting within supply chain management. Explore quantitative approaches employed in supply chain planning for data-driven decision-making. Delve into qualitative approaches utilized in planning to consider non-numeric factors impacting the supply chain. Comprehend the fundamentals of Supply Chain Analytics. Analyze the nature and advantages of Supply Chain Stimulation. Apply various simulation techniques in the context of Supply Chain Management. Understand the concept and implications of the Bullwhip Effect in supply chains. Evaluate the dynamic elements inherent in Supply Chain dynamics. Implement Monte Carlo Simulation Models in the context of supply chain scenarios. Utilize Agent-based Models for simulating and analyzing supply chain processes. Apply Cluster Analysis methodologies within the realm of Supply Chain dynamics. Implement Facility Location Methods to optimize supply chain networks. Understand the Concept, Types, and Importance of Inventory and Inventory Control. Grasp the Concept and Structure of Inventory Management. Analyze the Components Involved in Inventory Control Decision-Making. Evaluate Inventory Management Performance Metrics for Effective Assessment. Comprehend the Concept of the Inventory Management System. Understand the Concept of Customer Service Levels in the Context of Inventory Management. Solve Problems Related to Inventory Management using the Concept of the Newsvendor Problem. Apply General Inventory Control Techniques, including the Square Root Law. Recognize the Role of Information Technology (IT) in Inventory Management. Apply Six Sigma Tools and Methodology for Process Improvement. Identify and Analyze Key Drivers of Supply Chain for Effective Management. Evaluate the Importance of Supply Chain Integration and Understand the Role of IT in Enhancing Supply Chain Management. Demonstrate Proficiency in Utilizing Supply-Chain-Management Software for Efficient Operations. Understand the concept of Supply Chain Risk Management. Identify and analyze various Supply Chain Risk Management Strategies. Evaluate the effectiveness of Incentive Alignment strategies in Supply Chain contexts. Describe the Five Pillars of Supply Chain Resilience and their significance. Analyze the role and impact of Outsourcing in Supply Chain Management. Differentiate between Lean Strategy, Agile Strategy, and Leagile Strategy in Supply Chain contexts. Explain the concept and implementation of Vendor Managed Inventory System. Understand the principles and benefits of Collaborative Planning, Forecasting, and Replenishment in Supply Chain management. Analyze the causes and consequences of the Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chain dynamics. Understand the operational dynamics of Tim Hortons through a comprehensive case study analysis. Identify and delineate the distinct roles and responsibilities of Operations Managers and Supply Chain Managers within organizational contexts. Define and distinguish between order winner and order qualifier concepts in supply chain management, and analyze their significance in competitive strategies. Evaluate the six critical trade-offs that CEOs encounter when managing the supply chain, recognizing their implications for strategic decision-making. Explore Hayes and Wheelwright's framework of the four stages of operations, including its application in assessing organizational maturity and strategic alignment. Participants will explore supply chain planning, forecasting models, and analysis tools for operational efficiency. The programme covers inventory control methods, the role of IT in supply chain management, and Six Sigma methodologies. Additionally, participants will learn risk management strategies, the concept of vendor-managed inventory, and sustainable operations practices through case studies. The course emphasizes the integration of advanced supply chain technologies and sustainability practices. After the successful completion of this course, you will understand the following; Supply Chain Planning: Supply Chain Planning Models and Approaches: Supply Chain Analysis Tools and Models: Inventory Control and Management Approaches: SCM Quality Management System Managing Supply Chain Risks and Alliances Sustainability in Supply Chain and Operations Management:
